title: developers.apideck.com/apis/crm/copper/connection
snippet:
- You need a Copper account on a plan that includes API access.
- You need to be a Copper **Admin**. Copper states that only Admin users can generate API keys. If you are not an Admin, ask one of your Copper Admins to generate the key, or to give you the Admin role.

Copper uses API key authentication. When you connect through Vault, your key and email address are sent as request headers on every call, as described in [Copper Developer API: requests and rate limits](https://developer.copper.com/introduction/requests.html):
```
X-PW-AccessToken: your-api-key
X-PW-Application: developer_api
X-PW-UserEmail: your-email-address
```
API keys carry no scopes. What the connection can read and write follows the key owner's permissions in Copper.

title: Copper
snippet:
Access requirements

| Partnership | ❓ | |
| App review | ❓ | |
| Security audit | ❓ | |

- Copper offers both OAuth and API_KEY authentication modes. To use OAuth2.0 with Copper, you must first register your application.
- To register your application, [contact](https://developer.copper.com/introduction/oauth/index.html#:~:text=To%20register%20your,all%20authorization%20flows.) copper.
- You will need to provide the name and purpose of your application as well as a URL to an HTTPS endpoint that will handle the secure callback. You will receive two credentials, client_id and client_secret, required for all authorization flows.
- To generate an API token, in the Copper web app navigate to `System settings` > `Integrations` > `API Keys` and click the `GENERATE API KEY` button.

title: Create an API key
snippet:
To access the Copper API, you need to have an API key. To create an API key, go to the [Copper Platform UI](https://platform.copper.co/) and follow these steps:
1
Go to organisation settings

Determine if the API key should be associated with your personal account or a service user account. Optionally, you can restrict its access to specific IP addresses by setting IP addresses restrictions.

title: Copper API review: contact caps and 180 a minute
snippet:
# every Copper Developer API call carries all three
X-PW-AccessToken: $COPPER_API_KEY
X-PW-Application: developer_api
X-PW-UserEmail: owner@yourcompany.com
# base: api.copper.com/developer_api/

Requests are limited to 180 a minute on a rolling window, the same on every plan that has the API. What the plan changes is how many contacts you may store: 2,500 on Basic, 15,000 on Professional, unlimited on Business.

Authentication is an API key sent in three custom headers, or OAuth 2.0 for applications other people install.

A Copper user's access can be restricted by team permissions, and the API honors those restrictions. Copper's own advice is to use an admin's credentials for integrations, and to create a separate, non-personal user so records written through the API are owned by the integration rather than by a person.
## Copper API pricing, plan by plan
Copper API pricing is seat pricing: the API comes with the subscription, and the plan you choose sets the contact cap rather than the request rate.
### Basic
$23
/seat/mo billed annually, $29 month to month
- 2,500 contact limit
- Pipelines and task automation
- Contact enrichment
### Professional
$59
/seat/mo billed annually, $69 month to month
- 15,000 contact limit
- Workflow automation, bulk email and reporting
- Integrations
### Business
$99
/seat/mo billed annually, $134 month to month
- Unlimited contacts
- Email series and custom reports
- Multi-currency and premium support

### API key
For individual users and your own integrations.
- Sent as X-PW-AccessToken, never as a Bearer token.
- Must travel with X-PW-UserEmail, the email of the user who made it.
- And with X-PW-Application: developer_api.
- HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or higher is required.
